# Library

## Identity and consulted witness

Pseudo-Apollodorus, Library, trans. James George Frazer. [Selected digital carrier](https://www.theoi.com/Text/Apollodorus3.html). Accessed and saved 8 September 2026. The raw response is retained at `working/sources-texts-references/primary-texts/attica/pseudo-apollodorus-library-frazer.html` (SHA-256 `07f6dab5c2a483aaa280dd9689e4acde477d49ef474d9aea562904b487b9da90`). A saved page can contain more material than the selected reading; no whole-work reading is claimed.

## Source-specific reading

The narrative first places the earth-born, serpent-human Cecrops and the name Cecropia before the gods’ competition. Poseidon produces his sea at the centre of the Acropolis; Athena calls Cecrops to witness her planting. Zeus appoints the twelve gods as arbiters, explicitly distinguishing competing accounts of the judges. Cecrops’s testimony grounds the award to Athena. The resulting city-name is followed by Poseidon’s flood of the Thriasian plain and Attica.

That order makes witnessing, arbitration, naming and force different acts. The paragraph supplies the whole contest without supplying Taylor’s olive-to-light transformation or a utilitarian test for preferring gifts. Its account of the judges must remain distinct from Hyginus’s Jupiter and Augustine’s citizens.
